kernels.definition: A beat is a regularly recurring pulse, and meter organizes recurring beats into groups while rhythm places durations and attacks within that framework.

definitionAnchor.quote: A beat is a pulse in music that regularly recurs.

facts.text: Duple meter groups beats in twos, triple meter groups them in threes, and quadruple meter groups them in fours.

anchor.quote: Duple meters have groupings of two beats, triple meters have groupings of three beats, and quadruple meters have groupings of four beats.

facts.text: In simple meter, each beat divides into two equal parts; in compound meter, each beat divides into three equal parts.

anchor.quote: Compound meters are meters in which the beat divides into three.

facts.text: In a simple-meter time signature, the top number gives the beats per measure and the bottom number identifies the note value used as the beat unit.

anchor.quote: the top number of a time signature represents the number of beats in each measure, while the bottom number represents the beat unit

facts.text: A measure contains one recurring beat group, and bar lines separate adjacent measures in notation.

anchor.quote: A measure is equivalent to one group of beats.

attribution: Open Music Theory by Mark Gotham, Kyle Gullings, Chelsey Hamm, Bryn Hughes, Brian Jarvis, Megan Lavengood, John Peterson, and contributors

mcItems.q: In a simple-meter time signature, what does the top number show?
op: How many beats are in each measure
Which note value gets one beat
How each beat splits into smaller parts
How many measures are in a phrase
mcItems.ex: The top number shows how many beats are in each measure. A common mix-up is to treat that number as the note value for the beat, but that role belongs to the bottom number in simple meter.

op: Each beat divides into two equal parts
Each beat divides into three equal parts
Beats are grouped in threes
Measures are marked by recurring pulse
mcItems.ex: Each beat divides into two equal parts in simple meter. The usual mistake is to confuse beat division with beat grouping; grouping in threes describes triple meter, not simple meter.

keyTerms.df: A regularly recurring pulse in music that helps organize timing.
keyTerms.eg: While listening, I counted the steady pulse that kept returning in the excerpt.
keyTerms.mi: It is the same thing as a measure.
keyTerms.cx: The pulse keeps coming back regularly, while a measure is a group of beats marked in notation.

keyTerms.df: A vertical notation mark that separates one measure from the next.
keyTerms.eg: On the score, the bar lines showed where one recurring beat group ended and the next began.
keyTerms.mi: It shows whether the meter is simple or compound.
keyTerms.cx: Meter type comes from how beats are grouped and divided, not from the bar line itself.
